reports.title: Motorola Solutions Reports Third-Quarter 2026 Financial Results

guidance.heading: BUSINESS OUTLOOK
section: •Fourth quarter 2026 - The company expects revenue growth of approximately 13% compared to the fourth quarter of 2025 and non-GAAP EPS between $5.47 and $5.52 per share. This assumes approximately 168 million of fully diluted shares and a non-GAAP effective tax rate of approximately 22.5%.

•Full-year 2026 - The company now expects revenue of approximately $13.050 billion, up from its prior guidance of $12.975 billion and non-GAAP EPS between $17.94 and $17.99 per share, up from its prior guidance of between $17.62 and $17.72 per share. This outlook assumes approximately 168 million of fully diluted shares and a non-GAAP effective tax rate between 21.5% and 22%.
In addition, the company is increasing its operating cash flow expectations to $3.050 billion for the full year.

desk.headline: Sales up 12% to $3.4bn and adjusted EPS $4.69, both beat; full-year outlook raised again but Q4 sales guide a touch below estimates
results: Sales rose 12% to $3.4bn, with both segments growing at double digits; acquisitions added $211m.
Adjusted EPS rose 16% to $4.69, but GAAP EPS fell 8% to $3.06 because of a bigger earnout charge for the Silvus deal.
Adjusted operating margin widened to 32.5% from 30.5%, despite higher supply-chain and memory chip costs.
Record Q3 orders pushed backlog to an all-time high of $16.6bn, up 14%.

Free cash flow fell to $589m on higher tax and interest payments; $200m paid in dividends, $94m in buybacks, and the buyback authorisation was raised by $2bn. The $1.3bn D-Fend counter-drone deal closed.

guidance.summary: Motorola raised its full-year revenue and adjusted EPS targets for the second time and lifted its cash flow target to $3.05bn. For Q4 it expects sales up about 13% and adjusted EPS of $5.47-5.52; as reported, the implied Q4 sales figure is slightly below analysts' estimate.

points: Orders were a record, up more than 20% from a year ago, across all three technology areas.
Memory chip costs of about $150-160m this year could roughly double in 2027; the company is answering with supplier deals and selective price increases.
Silvus (military radio networks) demand shows no sign of slowing, with about 30% growth expected next year; D-Fend counter-drone is being folded into public-safety offerings.
CEO Greg Brown said public-safety funding remains strong; the CFO noted a roughly $75m tariff refund benefit will not repeat in 2027.
Nearly all customers are said to pick the premium tier of the company's AI assistant products.
call.source: Call coverage: GuruFocus via Yahoo Finance, 5 Nov 2026; StockStory via TradingView (no prepared remarks filed)

watch: How much of the expected doubling in memory costs price increases can offset in 2027.
Whether Q4 sales land near the ~13% growth target, given the guide sat a little under estimates.
Integration of D-Fend and Silvus growth in drone and defence markets.
